utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning to everybody in the courtroom and everybody in the booths; good morning to the Prosecution and Defence counsels. Let us take up our proceedings. But before we have the witness called in, I should like to inform you, and I think Mr. Krstan Simic has already been informed of the fact that there has been a ruling, a decision, that is, the Victims and Witnesses Unit. Have you been informed of that, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes. I have received the protection of witnesses decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The decision was dated the 25th of January, but you have the floor anyway now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence calls witness Dragan Popovic to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dragan Popovic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are now going to read the solemn declaration handed to you by the usher. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please draw closer to the microphone. Let me start off by thanking you for coming to the Tribunal. You're going to be answering questions put to you by Mr. Krstan Simic, who you know already. He is the gentleman standing to your left, of course. Mr. Simic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Good morning to you too, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you state your full name and surname, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you give us your exact date of birth.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The 25th of October, 1964, in Gradina, Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is that your place of residence today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I live in Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I completed primary school, not secondary school, but I attended two courses, one for postmen organised by the post office, and one for the railways.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have a daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I did my military service from the 1st of November, 1984 until the 25th of December, 1985.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, where were you employed up until the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in Croatia, in Zagreb, to be exact, where I actually lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did your family live with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my father, my sister, my wife, and my child. We all lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Prior to the war conflict, did you leave Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you leave with your family or alone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I had to leave alone first, and my family came seven months later. I had no news of my family during those seven months.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of 1992, according to the present system that prevailed, were you mobilised, called up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where was your war assignment? That is to say, what were your duties within this mobilisation, call-up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was first in the 43rd Motorised Brigade of Prijedor, and then I was on the battle front at Lipik, at the front at Lipik, but for a short period of time, just one month. After that, I reported back to Prijedor, to the military department there, and they gave me another assignment, which was the department of the Omarska Police Station, the Omarska Police Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In the Omarska Police Department, did you have the status of reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, as a reserve police officer, did you have the task, with other policemen, of providing security for the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: We were told it was an investigation centre of Omarska, and that was where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who gave you that assignment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The head of the police department in Omarska, Zeljko Meakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the period of time you spent on that assignment, given to you by Mr. Meakic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I can't quite remember but I think it was from the 29th of May up until the beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was that 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: How did you -- how were you on duty? How was duty work organised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: We had three shifts, so I worked for 12 hours and then I was off for 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the time the camp was in existence, did you have any leave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, twice. I had leave from the camp twice.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Just slow down, please, and make pauses.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When were you absent for the first time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The first time I was absent was after an incident that occurred to me personally down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How long were you absent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was absent for about nine or ten days, the first time, the first time I was absent, it was of a nine to ten day duration.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What month was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: It was in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly when your absence began and how long it lasted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly, but it was from the 10th of December -- the 10th or the 12th of June until the 19th or 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said that you were absent on another occasion, absent from the camp. When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: That was when my family arrived from Zagreb, and that was from about the 7th of July up until the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where was your family accommodated when they came back from Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: With my in-laws in Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How far is Prnjavor from Omarska and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: It was about 80 kilometres away from Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who gave you permission to absent yourself in July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I first contacted Zeljko Meakic the chief of the Omarska Police Department, and he probably asked for authorisation from Prijedor because it wasn't in his -- part of his competence to be able to give -- to allow me leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Why were you granted permission to absent yourself in July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was permitted to do so because I hadn't seen my wife and child for seven months.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where were they during those seven months?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: They were in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: During that time, were you able to talk to your wife and child at any point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any information as to how they were, whether they were alive and well, whether they had anything to eat, whether they were safe?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I had no information about them whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the two periods that you were absent in July 1992, how many shifts did you spend in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I did about 15 shifts, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You've already said that when you were absent the first time, and your absence lasted about nine days, that was in June, you said that it had to do with an incident that you personally took part in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What happened? Why were you absent? What did you do for those nine days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was being investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who conducted the investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The inspectors from Prijedor. I didn't know them. They conducted the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was the investigation about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: An incident occurred. As I said, I took part in it personally. I came on duty to do my shift at around 1900 hours, and at about 2200 hours, a man who was prisoner there, actually one of the detainees, one of the prisoners -- what did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that in a moment. Let's just take it step-by-step. That particular evening when the incident occurred, where were you doing guard duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was on duty beside the administration building towards the "white house," that side. In front of the restaurant, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to hear, the exact location. Now, that particular post, was there anybody else of the reserve police force on duty there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Dudo Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was his status?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He was also a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where was he standing on duty on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: That night, he left the guard post. He went home when we transferred shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he ask anybody whether he could go home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. The chief of the Omarska Police Station wasn't there, and whenever he wasn't there, then people did what they liked and would go home when they liked.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I should like now to go back to the incident itself, and could you try and be as precise as possible and concise as possible in giving your answer. Could you try and describe to us what happened on that particular occasion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: As a guard, I was alone. It was night-time, and suddenly I saw some commotion going on in the restaurant. I went up to the window because there were some open windows to let the air in. So I went up to the window, and I saw a man get up and shout, "People, we have to escape from here. We're human beings. This is not the proper place for us," he said. And the people showed him that I was standing there, that I was a guard and I was standing there. And then he said, "Well, why are you afraid of the guards?" Then he cursed me and my mother and my child, and he said, "I'll slit the guard's throat and then the road is open to the rest of you." I cautioned him. I cautioned that gentleman. I don't know his name. I said, "Sir, remain calm. Don't try and do anything." But he moved towards me. There was a chair in between us. He took up the chair and wanted to throw it out of the window towards me. I was afraid. I was alone. There was nobody else around. And I tried to warn him again, and I got hold of my rifle, and I wanted to shoot up in the air to caution him to stop. However, the bullet hit the man. I don't quite know how myself. After that, I heard that two other people were wounded. I'm very sorry that that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Please try and collect yourself. Take a rest, and we'll continue. Were you actually targeting the man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I had no intention of shooting at him. I wanted to shoot up in the air, but as I shot from my hip, the bullets went up into the ceiling and probably ricocheted downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How do you know that the bullets hit the ceiling?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The next day, when I was in Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether anybody told you that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The inspectors in Prijedor told me that during the investigation that they conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: At the moment you fired, were you in front of the restaurant building, alone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: After the shooting and that accident, did other guards come up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Several guards ran up to see what was going on, and Zeljko Meakic, the commander of the police station, was there too, and he called an ambulance to have the injured transported. After that, he put me into a car and took me off to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When the chief of the police department arrived, Mr. Meakic, with the other guards, amongst those guards was there an active policeman by the name of Miroslav Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. Miroslav Kvocka was not on duty that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that after having been -- after the injured were transported by the ambulance as organised by Mr. Meakic, that you went to Omarska with Mr. Meakic. Could you tell us where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: We went to a cafe. We had a cup of coffee so that I could calm down. That's what he said, that I should calm down and report to the police station in Prijedor the next morning at 9.00, which is precisely what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What happened the following day at the police station where you reported, as you said a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: They conducted an investigation. They questioned me, asked me how it happened. I said I was very frightened and that I couldn't -- and I'm still afraid today. I'm extremely sorry that it came to that, that it took place at all. And I told them that they should go and ask the detainees and conduct their investigations there and to ask the people who were injured how it all happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you questioned a number of times, interrogated a number of times during that investigation period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was questioned on several occasions over a period of two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the investigators? Did you know their names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were they people who had come to the Omarska camp, who were investigators in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We did not -- the transcript has not recorded your final answer. The people who interrogated you in Prijedor, were they the same investigators who worked in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know those investigators. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see them in Omarska? Were they investigators in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see some of them but not all of them. Some of them were but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't think you understand me. Listen to my question again. The people who interrogated you in Prijedor, did you see them performing the interrogations at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw some of those people in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did they -- what did the investigators tell you finally?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: At the end, the investigators said that they had conducted the investigation, that they had gone on the spot to Omarska, to investigate the matter, that they talked to one of the detainees - I think his name was Dedo Crnalic - they talked to him and he confirmed my story, and that one of the injured people also confirmed my story. They told the inspectors the same thing that I had told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: After that, did you return to do your -- to do your security detail work in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I had ten days off. And after that, they asked me to return to my guard post in Omarska, to do my guard duty there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to the beginning for a moment. When Mr. Meakic gave you your assignment, together with the other police officers, to provide security, did he tell you how long this would last?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They told us that this assignment would last for about ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago but let me ask you: Did you know a policeman Miroslav Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was he on duty at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He was. He did the same duties that I did. He had the same duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How often did you see him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Not very often, because I was absent while Miroslav Kvocka was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kvocka appear at the beginning to provide security for the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your own absence, can you tell us roughly -- or, rather, did Mr. Kvocka stay until the camp existed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. Miroslav Kvocka left after my return -- two or three days after my return from my absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And you didn't see him again in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: After -- when I returned, I saw him perhaps two or three times again but not after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In addition to yourself, was there any other security in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The army provided security for the camp as well, but outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What about inside the compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a special police unit from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know who their commander was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it Mr. Zeljko Meakic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. They had their own commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How long did they stay on in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: They were there for about a fortnight and they worked in two shifts. They had two commanders in fact. Each shift had its leader, two leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you have any other superior officer apart from Mr. Meakic, whom you said was the chief of the police department?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, do you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What is your nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: My nickname is Pavlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do people know you by your nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody in Omarska and the surrounding parts call me by my nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And my last question: Did you personally, during those 15 shifts that you did in Omarska, take part in any other incident that took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, but I did hear about another incident taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, we have discussed these events two or three times. I should like -- you asked you said you would like to give us your motives for appearing before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, when you say, "We have already discussed these events," what do you mean by "we"? Who is "we"?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovic and myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was your motive? When everybody who is not in contact with Omarska, people don't like to come to the Tribunal, why have you come here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I have come to the Tribunal because I don't feel guilty. I am extremely sorry that the incident took place, and I wanted to tell the truth about the incident which had happened and to tell the truth about everything that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are there any other Defence counsel who would like to intervene? Mr. Nikolic? Yes, Mr. Nikolic. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My name is Zarko Nikolic, and I represent the accused Milojica Kos in this case. I should like to ask several questions of you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please do, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us if you know the person by the name of Milojica Kos?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you know Milojica Kos from before the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Milojica Kos is from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I think he's from the village of Donja Lamovita. I mean, I know he's from that village, which is located some 3 or 4 kilometres from Omarska in the direction of the village of Kevljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know what is Milojica Kos' occupation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He's a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I will use the term that you yourself used in this context, and I should like to ask you whether in the investigation centre in Omarska you worked together with Milojica Kos.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know what Milojica Kos did in the investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He was also a reserve police officer, as myself, in the investigation centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know what his function was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't have any functions whatsoever. He was a simple guard like myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your knowledge, was Milojica Kos authorised to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He was not able to issue any orders to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, did Milojica Kos have any subordinate individuals in the investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you and Milojica Kos work in the same shift?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And my last question. I just want to be sure I understand you correctly. You said that the only superior individual to you was the commander of the police station in Omarska, Zeljko Meakic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions to ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Nikolic. Any other Defence counsel who would wish to intervene? No. Thank you very much once again, Mr. Nikolic. I believe that Mr. Waidyaratne will conduct the cross-examination of this witness. Mr. Popovic, you will now be answering questions that the counsel for the Prosecution, Mr. Waidyaratne, is going to ask of you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, could you tell us how you came to the camp when you reported to work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was assigned to the camp by the commander of the police station in Omarska. He was the one who took me there, and he told me that it was an investigation centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Then after that, how did you come? Were you taken in a bus to the camp or did you come on your own?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: We went there in a van.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So the reserve policemen who had to report for a certain shift was transported in a kombi or a van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And the person whom you referred to as Mr. Meakic, the Commander of the Omarska Police Station, he came separately. He had a car. Did you see that car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that, but I said that he was the Commander of the Omarska Police Station -- of the police department and not of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see him come to the camp in a car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes he would come in a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Kvocka coming in a car, a green Mercedes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. He had a car of his own, a privately-owned car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: He came to the camp in his own car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him coming in his own car on two occasions. At least I thought it was his car, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, very quickly I will ask you some basic questions. When you were working in the camp, you said that you had to work 12 hours and you were off 24 hours. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when you reported for these shifts, how many people were there with you in one shift?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Twenty people, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And you were all given specific assignments. If I may give an example, you were given a certain place to guard or stand and guard. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who gave those instructions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The Commander of the police station department in Omarska, Zeljko Meakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When Mr. Meakic was not there, who gave you those orders or places to stand or what to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: We already -- we were already assigned our guard posts by the Commander, Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Say, for instance, one day somebody was absent and you had to cover up that area too, who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody gave me orders. I would only take over my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That is correct, but --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: And I would take the duty of the person who was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: On your own? Nobody asked you to do that or stand in place of the other person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it went. Everybody proceeded in the usual way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when you reported to work, did you all have a roll-call?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. We only had one roll-call. That was the first time when we arrived, when we were given our assignments, so that we already knew where to go when we came to report for duty. We knew exactly which guard posts we were assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, the time that you spent in the camp, you said 15 shifts. Did you have to do --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: -- only the guard duty or were you given any other assignments?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Only the guard duty. When I was on those 15 shifts, that was the only duty I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Popovic, can you tell the Chamber as to where you stood guard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I stood guard in front of the restaurant, in the administration building, on the other side of the "white house." I mean the place that they refer to as the "white house".

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Is it closer to the "white house" or away from the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: It really depended on the agreement between me and my colleague Dudo Jokic. Sometimes he would be closer to the place and I would be down there. It really depended on how we would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Generally if Jokic was there, where would you stand? For example, if Jokic was there, where would you stay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Jokic would be at one corner and I would be at the other corner or the other way round.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So you changed places.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was our mutual agreement between the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, what -- what was the weapon that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was given an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And how many rounds or ammunition was given to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I had one clip containing 30 bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How were you dressed? Were you in uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a blue uniform, the one that was usually worn by reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Other than Mr. Meakic whom you mentioned, who were the others in your shift?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kos was with me, Mr. Milenko Jasnic, then Rajko Marmat. I can't remember all of them, because I had lived in Zagreb for 12 years and I didn't know people in the area very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The person whom you mention as Rajko, is it Rajko Marmat, who was the reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you told that you were given instructions as to where you should stand and what you should guard. Did anyone give you instructions as to what you should do and what you should guard? What were you there to guard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: We provided security, both to the detainees -- well, mostly to the detainees. We were their security personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did the person who provided -- were you instructed as to what you should do if one of these detainees misbehaved or misconducted themselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any instructions. I mean, Meakic told us to call someone who was -- if anything happens, who was in the vicinity and to report to him, and if he was not there, to try and calm down the situation, if there is any tension or something going on, as I tried to do in that incident that I described. But that man came up to me, and I was -- I panicked. I was alone, it was night, and there were no other guards in my vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have not come -- I am not asking you about the incident. I'm just asking you in general. We will talk about the incident after. Now, Mr. Popovic, when Mr. Meakic was not there, whom would you look for to take instructions or to discuss something? Who was the next senior person in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody was the next senior person in the camp. We always tried to call him. We had his telephone number where he could be reached, and he would come and deal with the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: If you know, did the detainees have any rules or regulation that they should adhere to during the time that they spent in the camp, as to how they should go to a place or how they should sit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: That happened only when they went to lunch. They would be lined up and they would go to lunch in columns, but otherwise, nobody prohibited them anything. Nobody told them where to sit and where not to sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who gave them the instructions when they went for lunch?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: One of the guards, one of us, who was in charge of that particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did the guards also give instructions to the prisoners and the detainees as to what time they should take to eat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. They went for lunch at the usual time and they were free to eat until they finished their meal. Actually, I don't know. I didn't work there where they ate their meals. I mean, inside that particular room, the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Popovic, you said that you were called or nicknamed Pavlic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What is the meaning of Pavlic? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: This nickname means a lot to me. I was nicknamed after my grandfather, whose name was Pavla and my younger brother is also called Pavla and that's why they called me Pavlic in my village. I got that nickname when I was very young, maybe seven years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you spoke about an incident concerning a shooting. Could you tell us, tell the Chamber, as to how many people were there in the restaurant - I'm talking about the detainees - approximately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe about a hundred, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And they were all seated when you saw this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Some of them were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, at the moment the incident happened, but the time that gentleman whom I killed unfortunately, when he asked them to run away, but at that moment they stood up. I didn't know what their intentions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you were outside the restaurant building, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And the person whom you say that you accidentally shot and killed was inside the building; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you subsequently find out as to the name of this person, the person, the deceased?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I learned that through the media. I learned about it in the papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know whether he was a young person or an old person, an elderly person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I still don't know that. I think he was middle aged, according to what I could tell at that moment. He could have been between 45, 50 years of age, according to my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you're a person who had served in the front and had training with regard to using of weapons; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never underwent any training except for the training that I had as part of my regular military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: But you knew how to handle a weapon? That's why it was given to you; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I learned in the regular army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you recollect as to when, which month, this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: It happened in June, between the 10th and the 12th of June, according to what I can remember. It was a long time ago. It's difficult to remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that there were many others who were injured due to this shooting. Did you -- and you said that you knew those people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question. Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovic didn't say at any moment that he knew the people who were injured, and he didn't say that many people were injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection rejected. Would you pursue with your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, did you get to know as to how many people were injured due to that shooting, this accidental shooting that you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I heard from the inspectors in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: That is, that there were two men, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know where they were injured, as to what injuries, where he had sustained the injuries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I didn't see that, because I left with Mr. Meakic but I heard that one of them -- that the bullet had grazed one of them on the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you learn the names of those people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you make an attempt to find out those names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I did try to find out but nobody knew, nobody told me. I tried to learn it from the inspector and the commander of the police station department in Omarska. Mr. Meakic, he told me that he would ask the investigators but nobody told me any name, though I would like to know their names so that I can publicly apologise to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You couldn't find still -- up to date, you have not been able to find the names of those people; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were questioned by the interrogators on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions during two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And the people, the interrogators, that you don't know their names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you get any report after this as a result of this investigation that you underwent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Only an oral report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you sign any statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I signed my statement, the one that I gave them, to the investigators, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And the result of this investigation was that you were never punished or reprimanded or warned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't receive anything after that, but I did expect to be punished because that is what I deserved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: After ten days, according to what you say, you returned to the same place to do the same duty. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Popovic, you were there during the time that you spent in the camp. Did you, by any chance, or take any interest, come to know why these people, the Muslim -- the detainees were brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I only heard stories from the Commander of the police station department in Omarska. We were told that they were supposed to give some statements to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: With regard to what, why were the detainees there, did you know why the detainees were there or was it common knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know. I didn't know why they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you discuss this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the same evening when they were brought in, we were not working yet. There were some police officers from Prijedor there. I know there was a rebellion in my village the same evening. People wanted to know why those people were being brought to the mine complex, and a decision was made. It was actually requested that the people be released. That was the kind of request that we sent to the municipality, municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, as a reserve policeman, did you sign a loyalty oath at the Omarska Police Station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand your question. Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, did you sign a loyalty oath as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I signed a loyalty oath to the fact that I would be discharging my duties honourably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: That was before, around the 30th of April, because prior to those events, I had already joined the reserve police force, and I stood guard in my village as a member of the local patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Before I conclude -- please bear with me. Two questions. When did you return from Zagreb to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in Omarska on the 20th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Then you served at the front in Lipik. That's what you said? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received call-up papers to that effect from the Ministry of Defence Department in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And when were you brought to the camp for the first time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: To the camp? I was brought to the camp on the 29th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And the last question. When were you mobilised in the Omarska Police Station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I said that already. Sometime around the 30th of April, 1992. I was mobilised to the police station in Omarska one month before that, and I was patrolling in my village during that period of time, the village of Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, about the shooting incident, and you spoke about a person by the name of Kos who was in your shift, was he present at the present time when this shooting took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: See, at that moment, I didn't recognise anyone. I was really beside myself. It's something that doesn't happen every day. It was a shock for me. I was completely lost at the moment, and I didn't see Mr. Kos anywhere around at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You mentioned the name of Dedo Crnalic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know that he was related to Miroslav Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know as to whether Dedo Crnalic is alive now or as to what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, but I wish he were alive. But I don't know what happened with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That concludes my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Waidyaratne. Mr. Simic, have you any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, would you please try and concentrate on the beginning of that unfortunate shooting, not the period that followed. Anyone in the area of the restaurant, were they present when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. At that moment, there was no one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic. No additional questions? Thank you. Judge Fouad Riad, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I have a few inquiries or clarifications to ask you, and I will try to start from the end, where you were talking to the Prosecutor. You just mentioned that there was a rebellion in your village the same evening the detainees were brought to the camp. Was this a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No. Then what was the rebellion for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: It was a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And the Serbs were having a rebellion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. The people raised a hue and cry about the detention of people. They didn't understand what it was all about, why it was happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Who was crying? You mean the Serbs were crying because the Muslims were detained?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. They were indignant why people were being arrested. They weren't crying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes. You say any word would serve. Does that mean that the detainees were residents of this village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, those prisoners were not residents of that village. They came from other villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So the rebellion was for detainees coming from other villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned that you did not -- that Mr. Zeljko Meakic was the commander of the police, and when the Prosecutor asked you who gave the orders in his absence, you said that everybody knew his work. Does that mean that when Meakic was not there, there was no commander, there was nobody in charge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: There was no commander because he was the only one who could issue orders to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was an institution, and when the commander was absent, nobody was commanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And were you a shift leader or just a member, one of the people of a shift, one member of a shift?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was just a reserve policeman in the Omarska department of the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Because I understood that you said that Mr. Kvocka was on the same grade as you. Did I understand rightly or was he superior to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. He had the same position, the only difference being that he was an active-duty policeman and I was a reserve policeman, but we had the same kind of duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mean he would not be above you or above any other guard, would not be giving orders to the guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He couldn't issue orders because then each one of us could have issued orders to other people. You had to know who was the one issuing orders, and it was Mr. Meakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And apart from Meakic, nobody else would give orders; the chiefs, the heads of shift, for instance, would give orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any shift leaders. We were all members of a shift. We were all on shift duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you did not work where the prisoners took their meals. I just noted that in your answer to the Prosecutor, but I understood before that, when the incident happened, when the shooting happened, it was in the restaurant. Wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I was on the outside of the restaurant, not inside where the food was being distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Speaking of this incident, you said the prisoner was killed by a shot in the ceiling. Was that the result of an inquiry, that the shot in the ceiling would kill a man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: That is what I was told by the inspectors in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were there other incidents like that during your stay there which happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I never saw any other such incident, but I did hear about another one, and this was a rumour, talk, among the guards about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... punishment to the other one, too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the other guards involved in that other incident but I did expect punishment. However, as I said, they questioned Mr. Crnalic and one of the wounded men. That is what they told me. They confirmed my story, that I got scared, that he was heading towards me. And I'm really very sorry. I probably would never do anything like that again, but when one is afraid, one loses control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And your coming here was mainly to express this honourable feeling of being sorry, or to say anything else for Mr. Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I have come to describe my own personal incident in the first place because I couldn't stand it any longer. I wanted to tell this honourable court the truth. As for Mr. Kvocka, there is not much I can say about him because I had little contact with him. As much as I know and as much as I was able to see him, and that was about five times, I'm able to tell you about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, very much.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you told us, I believe, that this incident took place around 2200 hours. At least, you said it was at night several times. I would take that to be about 10.00 at night. And you said that there were 100, you estimated about a hundred people in the restaurant. Now, was that usual, in your experience as a guard, for there to be a hundred people, detainees, in the restaurant at 10.00 at night? Were they eating their meal or what at 10.00 at night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, they slept there at night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. These were people who were put up in the restaurant at night from -- okay. You also said that you shot into the air in order to scare -- or you thought you were shooting into the air in order to scare the person who was threatening to throw the chair through the window. You said you were on one side, you were outside the building, there was a window, and the detainees were inside. Now, the window was open?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The window that the man wanted to throw a chair through was not open but there were other open windows of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So when you shot your gun up into the air, did you -- you had to shoot through a window in order for it to get inside. So did you aim the gun through the window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I fired from the hip through the glass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't hear you say that, but I'm glad to be informed about that now. So you fired the bullet through the window in order to scare, in order to try to scare. Did you use more than one bullet or was it only one shot that you fired?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I fired a short burst of fire and the inspectors later told me -- because Zeljko seized the gun away from me and handed it over to the inspectors. They told me that in the clip, three rounds were missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. So three bullets. All right. Now, I want to make sure I understand your testimony about how the guards worked in Omarska. Were there -- there were shifts, right? I mean, there was -- there were shifts, people came at one time and they left at another time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand your testimony to say there were no shift commanders that you knew about. Is that right? Even though we have had many, many witnesses come and tell us about there being shifts and there being a commander for each shift, but you say that was not true when you worked there; is that right? There were no shift commanders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have a shift commander. My only commander was Zeljko Meakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. On the night of the incident, when you said Meakic came and he took the gun away from you and an ambulance was called to take the wounded people away, did you stay there until the ambulance had already come and taken the wounded away? Were you still there when they were removed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. Zeljko had driven me away prior to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That's my question. So you were telling us that after these persons had been, one killed, wounded, and an ambulance had been called, that Meakic took you in his car away back to Omarska, leaving nobody in charge on the camp. I mean, the detainees were still inside the restaurant, presumably, the wounded were still outside, and nobody was in charge. Everybody would just do what they thought was the right thing to do while he took you home or while he took you back to Omarska in the car.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: You see, I was quite beside myself. I can't remember exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Just then I wished I was dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand. But to the best of your memory, given the trauma of the circumstances, you don't remember that Meakic left anybody in charge of that scene with the wounded still waiting to be picked up and the detainees who had been -- in your view, being asked to revolt still being in the restaurant? You don't remember his leaving anybody in charge; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but probably he did. He could have chosen any reserve policeman or an active duty policeman if he happened to be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But you don't remember which one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you talked about your being told that the investigators spoke to two detainees, I mean one wounded and Mr. Crnalic. Did you hear whether or not they spoke to other people besides those two detainees, and to you, of course? I mean, did you hear whether they spoke to other guards, to other detainees, to Mr. Meakic, anyone else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Meakic was with me while I was being investigated in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you don't know whether they spoke -- they asked him what he had seen and what he knew about the incident separately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: They probably did, but I didn't see them do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my last question to you is: Several times, once from your own counsel and I think once in answer to one of Judge Riad's questions, you referred to hearing about another incident but in neither case, did you tell us what that incident was. Could you tell us briefly what this other incident you heard about was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody asked me about that other incident, when I mentioned it here in court. You're the first one to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: No, I know you're right. You're absolutely right. I understand that. That's why -- but I am asking you because, since it was -- obviously it stayed in your memory. I would like to know what it was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: You see, on that day, I was on duty in the hangar. I was assigned by Zeljko to keep watch duty in the hangar and, suddenly, shooting was heard. It was almost dark. And I heard a moan. There were three of us guards up there in the hangar. And then one of us, I think his name was Cica, Mico or something like that, he went off to see what was happening. When he came back, he said that a drunken man had come, that buses had arrived, bringing Muslims from somewhere, and that that man had started shooting at the buses, and that he heard that Mr. Kvocka had, on that occasion, grabbed the gun away from this drunken man, that he had run out and grabbed it from him. I wasn't there. I wasn't an eye witness, but I heard this story, that Mr. Kvocka had acted very bravely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Wald. Mr. Popovic, I have a few questions too for you. My first is, if I understood you well, during that month you knew nothing about your wife and child. You never heard them, their voices even. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I said no in the sense that I never heard anything about them, any news of them, because telephone lines were down then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When were the lines reconnected?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I saw my family for the first time after that when they arrived from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you saw your family around the 7th of July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, around that date. Whether it was the 7th or the 8th, I'm not sure. I asked to go away to Prnjavor on the 7th and I went there on the 8th, so that must be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you came from Zagreb on the 20th of October, 1991, did you tell your family where you were going?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: You see, Your Honours, there were threats by phone, words to the effect, "Why aren't you getting out, you Chetnik? You have no place here. This is a Croatian state." And as there was no way to reach Bosna, I fled to my uncle's place in Slovenia. I spent 15 days there. When I heard that the roads were open --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to interrupt you. You told your family that you were going to Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They knew I was going to Slovenia, but then I returned to Zagreb again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After Slovenia you went to Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I went to Bosnia. From Slovenia I returned to Zagreb and from Zagreb I went to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your family as was aware of your movements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: My family could not know anything about me in detail, just as I didn't know anything about them, but they knew that I was leaving because I had been threatened. I had no choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How did you learn that your family had arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: By my wife's mother. She let me know that they had arrived, because her mother, my mother-in-law, was living in Prnjavor, and they went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have already told us that there were other incidents when people were killed. Do you know how many such incidents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I know about the one I was involved in and this other one that I've just told you about, but I also know that when we first arrived, the first time I took up my duty, I saw four bodies, three or four. I think there were four corpses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was it a frequent occurrence in the camp for you to see bodies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. That was the only time I saw any bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only that one time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, only then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where were those bodies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Near the "white house." Between the "white house" and my guard post, roughly. So near the restaurant or between the restaurant and the "white house."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So all in all, for the 15 shifts more or less that you had, there were two incidents with firearms and shooting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is my incident and the incident with this drunkard who opened fire on the bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know who informed you about the results of the inquiry into your case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You told us that investigators spoke to you about the results of the inquiry into your incident with the shooting. Did I understand you right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who conveyed to you those results, the results of the inquiry?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: The inspector in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did this inspector work in Omarska as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that inspector did work in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where did he give you this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He gave it to me in Prijedor, in the police station there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. In Prijedor, not in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in Omarska, in Prijedor, because I went there on two consecutive days, and the second day he told me that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That day -- do you remember what day that was? What was the date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the day or the moment when he informed you, had you already resumed your duties when you were informed about these results, those ten days later that you went back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was informed two days after the incident. So I went to be interrogated on several occasions over two days, and then on the second day they told me I could go home, that I would be under investigation, and that they would let me know whether I could go back to work or go to detention, and then I was informed that I could go back to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So one day you went to Prijedor for the interrogation, and the second day they told you of the results of the inquiry; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they told you to wait at home, and they would call you to go back to work.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, or they would decide -- they said that they would investigate all the circumstances and make a ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I see you went back to work on the 19th or the 20th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who told you that you could go back to work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was informed by Zeljko Meakic, the Commander of the police station department, because he had probably been informed about it by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just then, did you get a gun or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was again issued a gun, but I was cautioned in future to take much greater care and think twice before deciding to use my weapon. Zeljko especially warned me of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this warning given to you the first time, when you were issued a weapon for the first time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody gave me any such warning on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was the weapon the same, by any chance, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received the same weapon with the same number on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another question. The reserve policeman were transported in a van. All the policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness didn't get an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is: You said that the reserve policemen were transported in a van. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the policemen or not all of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Both the reserve and the active-duty policemen were transported in a van to the Omarska Investigation Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zeljko Meakic, did he travel in that van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, not then. He came in his own car, a green Mercedes. His own car, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about Mr. Kvocka? Was he transported in that van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That evening, he was in the van, though later he came in his own private car on occasion. Not always, but sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From time to time. I see. Do you remember what kind of car he had, that he used, what kind of car it was, his private car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't have a driving licence. I never drove a car, so I don't know much about cars, I'm afraid. But I know that he would come mostly using a private car when he was bringing parcels for the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that there were at least 20 guards in the Omarska camp. Is that number correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. About 20 in a shift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. You had a gun. Did you have a mobile phone or a Motorola or something for communication purposes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I did not, but I heard that in the administration building there was a telephone and a radio receiver, but I didn't see that because I had nothing to do there. Actually, I did see it once when I went to ask Zeljko for permission to leave because my family had arrived, and it was then that I did see a telephone and two women typing something on a typewriter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So spontaneously you said, "I did not have any such devices." Did other guards have a Motorola or any other means of communication?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any guard on active duty or a reserve policeman having any such device.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dragan Popovic, you have pledged to tell us the truth and the whole truth. I want to ask you something. If there is a problem in the camp and Zeljko Meakic is not present, you have a problem, Zeljko Meakic is not there, how could you communicate with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: I would go up there where the telephone was and try to call him. There was a number there, the number of the police station department, because the camp was quite a distance away from the police station, and I would call up the policeman on duty to inform Zeljko, for him to take action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So each of the 20 guards, if there was a problem, as there was no commander in the camp, he would have to go to this telephone to communicate with Zeljko Meakic. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Anyone could reach that telephone and call up Zeljko should a problem arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there was no single person who coordinated the work of the 20 guards who were scattered all over the camp, is that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: While I was there, there was no such person. I don't know whether there was later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So each of the guards out of the 20 was his own commander. Is that your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't his own commander. We were just ordinary guards. But you see that we did communicate with Zeljko. He was our only commander. We had no one else to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not doubting what you are telling us. You are telling us that Zeljko Meakic was the commander. But when Zeljko Meakic was not there, there was no commander. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: Zeljko wasn't absent all that often from the camp. He was there very often. At night, you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for interrupting you, Mr. Popovic. Did Zeljko Meakic live and reside in the camp? Was he in the camp 24 hours, round the clock?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN POPOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't always there for 24 hours, but he did have a room with a bed in it. That is what they told me. I didn't see it. But I would see him often during the day and the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
